# Scrib SU -- 2026-09-02

Scheduled 10:00 CDT (15:00 UTC). The transcript runs 00:00:22 to 00:22:28 and
the recording metadata puts it at 15:00:09 to 15:22:44 UTC, so about 23
minutes. Eight speakers. Matthew Kaplan is on the invite but does not appear
in the transcript, so the attendee list above is who spoke, not who was
invited.

Two transcription artifacts worth knowing before reading quotes below. Karuna
Arshakota opens with "this is Vikash", and Rob refers to "the Jira board for

## Summary

Rob gave his own update first: he built a prototype section in the wiki
covering the flows and every individual screen (at-a-glance, screenshot, iOS
renders, features, data calls, components), and his goal today is to push that
into Jira as epics and features, with user stories to follow later. He also
opened a permanently-available Teams channel he calls office hours in the
Scribl Dev team, and offered to move the meta repo into the Scribl GitHub org
by renaming the Bounteous-named repo there.

Access is nearly closed out. Pramod confirmed GitHub and Apple developer
invites landed; Eric said AWS should finish today and that Apple approval came
quickly. Pankaj created a new Scribl mobile app repo without Bounteous in the
name, ported the earlier generated code into it, confirmed the monorepo
decision from yesterday, and set up branches. He is blocked on branch
protection rules: GitHub says the org needs a Team upgrade. Eric offered to do
whatever is needed once Pankaj emails him instructions. Nitish updated the
schema after yesterday's call and is now on the API contracts, which he will
commit and hand to Rob and Pankaj for review. Karuna is on the automation
framework, settled internally on a single repository for it, and is generating
test cases from the Lucid mock screens and the workflows now on the wiki page.
Shubhankar got admin rights on his machine yesterday, did his tool setup and a
code review of Pankaj's work, and is waiting on requirement clarifications he
raised with Rajeev before he can move into development.

Rob then walked the list of items left over from yesterday and closed all four.
Monorepo confirmed. Auth goes with Cognito now, built so a later shift to
WorkOS stays possible if enterprise SSO is ever wanted. Story text is
mandatory with no minimum length. And there is no draft-and-resume for
in-progress drawings. One new question opened: whether
the number of walls a user can create is capped, which Eric took away to
confirm by end of day.

## Questions / decisions

### Decisions

- Auth uses Cognito for now, not WorkOS. Cognito is faster to stand up and the team already knows it; WorkOS would add roughly one to two days of setup plus one to two days of development. Enterprise SSO is not in scope, so the simpler option wins (owner: Rob Forshier II, proposed by Pankaj Aggarwal, agreed by Eric Rice).
- The build must stay portable off Cognito: generate internal user IDs rather than depending on the Cognito sub UUID, or keep an internal mapping ID, so a later migration to WorkOS is possible (owner: Pankaj Aggarwal, endorsed by Rob Forshier II as "let's just make sure that we're future-proofing it").
- Story text is mandatory when posting, with no minimum length. A user who does not want to write can type a single character and move on (owner: Eric Rice).
- No draft-and-resume for in-progress drawings. Eric said a draft "isn't necessary at this point"; a state save across a screen switch is a nice-to-have, and Rob was explicit there is no "save come back to it later" (owner: Eric Rice, confirmed by Rob Forshier II).
- The app repo is a monorepo, closing yesterday's open item (owner: Pankaj Aggarwal).
- Test automation lives in a single repository rather than being split out. Thin: Karuna reported this as already settled in an internal QA discussion ("had some analysis and internal discussions like today, so we are going with the single repository for everything") without naming who decided it, so treat her as the reporter, not the owner.
- The meta repo moves into the Scribl GitHub org, by renaming the existing Bounteous-named repo there (owner: Rob Forshier II, agreed by Pankaj Aggarwal).
- App code lives in a new Scribl mobile app repo created without Bounteous in the name, so it can become the production repo (owner: Pankaj Aggarwal).

### Questions

- Is the number of walls a user can create capped in the MVP? Eric's working answer is a personal wall plus one group wall, with unlimited walls behind a premium subscription, but he is confirming with the Scribl team because pricing and monetization are still being worked out (raised by Karuna Arshakota, answer due 2026-09-02).
- What exactly does the GitHub org need for branch protection rules? Pankaj hit an error saying the org must be upgraded to GitHub Team, while Eric says payment is already set up on the account. Unresolved on the call; Pankaj is checking and will send instructions (raised by Eric Rice; Pankaj Aggarwal surfaced the upgrade-to-Team error and is investigating, rather than co-raising the question).
- What is the immediate requirement scope versus what belongs in the MVP? Shubhankar raised this against the Lucid board and Pankaj's code, and is waiting on Rajeev (raised by Shubhankar Bhavsar).
